title: The Receiving Authority
passages:
Fenn's rig didn't announce itself. No horn, no hail on the open channel — just the crunch of tires on the chalk line and the diesel cough settling into idle. The pump hall's big doors stood open on the grade, Saul's pencil frozen mid-tally on the clipboard, six scrubber cases already strapped to the pallet jack and the other five waiting their turn. Brill stood with her arms folded, lamp light catching the grease on her jaw, watching the rig's cab door swing down.

Fenn stepped out in the same coat they'd worn at Anza, badge catching the first light. No sidearm visible, no backup visible. Just the serve order folded in their gloved hand and the look of someone who'd already decided how the morning went.

"Didn't think you'd make the grade before eight," Kass said from the pallet jack. Their voice carried flat across the concrete, no surprise, no welcome.

Fenn didn't look at them. Eyes tracked the stacked cases, the dies on the workbench — Voss's square brass and the chipped crescent Ospina had brought down — then settled on the back room door where Voss had disappeared twenty minutes ago. "Desk's terms didn't change. Produce the forger or surrender the witness. First light was the deadline."

"First light's here," Ospina said. They stood by the reader cradle, live ring still hot from the crimp against Voss's die. The counter on their flagged authority blinked red in the reader's display, a wound that wouldn't close. "We've got eleven cases matched to two dies. The resealer's in the back. The witness is on the set."

"Freight is not a record." Fenn unfolded the serve order, the paper stiff with cold. "Red score is Anza sheltering a contested man. Eleven cases clean or dirty doesn't move the board. You put a forger on the plate or you put Marlowe in my rig. My clearance turns at eight. When it does, the reclamation unit rolls and I write this hall off the line."

Fenn tapped the wall reader's clock display with one gloved finger. The green numbers burned 07:56. "Four minutes. Starting now."

"Standing offer holds," Fenn added, voice dropping to the register that closed deals. "Full compressor power for the brother the hour the sister signs the witness over. That's the only trade the desk recognizes."

Rhea's name wasn't in this room. She was back at Anza relay shop, hand-pumping Ivo's respirator, two cartridges left. But the weight of it landed on Kass's shoulders anyway, visible in the way their jaw tightened.
